official.deadline_note: No central student deadline exists: each EMJM consortium sets and publishes its own. The Commission states that in most cases applications are submitted between October and January for courses starting the following academic year.
official.application_cycle: Annual intake - a new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the catalogue each year; applications are typically submitted between October and January for courses starting the following academic year
official.status_note: Rolling annual scheme for students: applications go directly to each selected programme and most deadlines fall between October and January for the following academic year. The EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue currently lists 218 projects.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Programme Guide: "Selected projects cannot charge student application fees. Moreover, projects cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to student participation in the course to Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders."
benefits: EU scholarship for individuals: EUR 1,400 per month (max. 24 months)
Full scholarships are available for the best students worldwide
Scholarships cover your participation costs and contribute to travel, visa, and a living allowance
The scholarship covers travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs
Scholarship holders are not charged tuition fees, other mandatory participation costs, or application fees
Scholarships are available that cover tuition fees, travel, and living costs (European Education Area)
eligibility: Have a bachelor's degree (first degree), or be in the last year of bachelor studies
Graduate before the master's programme starts
Bachelor's equivalent level of learning is also accepted if officially recognised, according to national legislation and practices, in the degree-awarding country
EMJMs enrol students at Master level who have obtained a first higher education degree or demonstrate a recognised equivalent level of learning

Students who have previously obtained an EMJM scholarship are not eligible to apply for an additional scholarship under the EMJM
An enrolled student and the EMJM consortium must sign a Student Agreement upon enrolment

Compulsory physical mobility for all enrolled students: minimum two study periods in two countries different from the student's country of residence, each at least one academic semester (30 ECTS, or at least 20 ECTS for 60-ECTS programmes)
selection_criteria: Selection, recruitment and monitoring of individual students fall under the sole responsibility of the EMJM consortium
Student selection must be organised transparently, impartially and equitably
EMJMs enrol excellent students worldwide; scholarships go to the best students applying
Geographical balance: no more than 10% of the total number of scholarships awarded during a project should go to candidates of the same nationality
coverage: Travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs
Participation costs, with tuition fees and other mandatory participation costs not chargeable to scholarship holders
A living allowance of EUR 1,400 per month for the duration of the programme (max. 24 months)
application_method: Students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme
Search the EACEA course catalogue for details of the latest programmes on offer
Each master's website sets out the course, participating universities, entry requirements and all steps of the application process (with and without scholarship)
The Erasmus Mundus Association provides course contacts, events and stories from successful applicants
official.application_route: Shortlist programmes in the EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue, then apply directly to each consortium via its own application form on the programme website, requesting the scholarship.
official.study_mode: full-time (the scholarship is awarded for full-time enrolment only)
official.citizenship_residency: Open to students from all over the world. For masters selected from 2021 the distinction between Programme and Partner countries no longer exists and all students receive the same scholarships.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - students from all over the world are eligible and nationality does not affect eligibility.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No limitation in terms of disciplines - EMJM proposals may cover any field of study.
official.duration: 1 to 2 academic years (12, 18 or 24 months; 60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits); the scholarship is granted for the full programme duration, maximum 24 months
official.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are high-level, integrated transnational study programmes at Master level, designed and delivered by an international consortium of at least three higher education institutions from three different countries, with compulsory physical mobility and either a joint or a multiple degree on completion. The EU funds these programmes and awards scholarships to the best students worldwide: EUR 1,400 per month covering travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs, with no tuition charged to scholarship holders.
official.region: Europe and beyond - study takes place at universities in several European and non-European countries
official.program_type: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM), Key Action 2 - Erasmus Mundus action, Lot 1

applicant_utility.summary: EMJM is not one scholarship but a family of 218 consortium-run masters, each with its own deadline (mostly October to January), its own portal and its own scholarship quota, so the real work is shortlisting programmes in the EACEA catalogue and submitting a separate, tailored application to each. Successful candidates receive EUR 1,400 a month for the full 12 to 24 months plus travel and installation support, and consortium members are barred from charging scholarship holders tuition or application fees. Because every consortium ranks applicants and awards its own scholarships, demonstrated fit with that specific programme's academic profile and mobility tracks matters more than any centralised cut-off.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year bachelor's students and recent graduates from any country who want a multi-country master's and will tailor one application per programme.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist 4-8 programmes in the EACEA catalogue and record each consortium's deadline, document list and scholarship quota from its own website.
Check whether each consortium accepts a Medium of Instruction certificate instead of IELTS/TOEFL - the rule differs by programme.
Build one master folder of scanned transcripts, degree certificate, CV and references, then re-package it per programme.
Start sworn translations or certified copies of non-English documents weeks ahead of each deadline.
Apply early in the October-January window; consortia close on their own dates, some as early as December.
common_rejection_risks: Missing a single consortium's earlier deadline because there is no central deadline to anchor on.
The 10% nationality cap per consortium makes applicants from heavily represented countries effectively face tougher odds.
Filing only the self-funded application and never activating the scholarship option on the form.
Prior degree content mismatching the programme's stated subject prerequisites.
Being a former EMJM scholarship holder - a second EMJM scholarship is not permitted.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The stipend is a fixed EUR 1,400 per month and travel/installation are capped lump contributions set by each consortium, so students in expensive cities, or supporting a family, may still need personal funds for housing deposits, insurance top-ups or dependants' costs.
document_audit: Each consortium asks for its own set - typically transcripts, a degree certificate, CV, motivation letter, references and proof of English - so never assume one pack fits all.
Sworn translations or certified copies of non-English documents are a frequent bottleneck close to deadlines.
Motivation letters must be programme-specific; generic text is a visible differentiator when consortia rank applicants.
alerts: The catalogue lists 218 projects, but not all still offer scholarships - confirm availability on the consortium page before investing effort.
The 12 February deadline in the Programme Guide is for universities applying to run an EMJM, not for students.
EACEA warns that EU scholarships are never granted for a fee - treat any site or agent demanding payment as fraudulent.
The scholarship requires full-time enrolment for its entire duration; part-time study is not compatible with the stipend.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit through each consortium's own online form on its programme website; the consortium itself ranks applicants, allocates its scholarship seats and issues results - the Commission runs no central student selection.
